 BOSSIER CITY, La. — Nestled just inside the gates of Barksdale Air Force Base, a staple of regional history continues to honor the brave service members of the ArkLaTex while showcasing decades of aviation power.
 The Barksdale Global Power Museum offers visitors an immersive look into military history, featuring dynamic indoor exhibits, historical artifacts, and community events that bring the past to life.
 Outdoors, the museum’s static aircraft display showcases impressive historic bombers, fighters, and reconnaissance planes that once dominated the skies, including the iconic B-52 Stratofortress.
 Whether exploring military artifacts or walking among giant warbirds, families and history enthusiasts across the ArkLaTex can experience the legacy of airborne defense right in their backyard.
 Anyone planning a visit to the Barksdale Global Power Museum should prepare ahead of time due to base security guidelines. Non-military visitors without a military sponsor or DoD ID must submit a Barksdale AFB Museum Access Pass form at least 30 days prior to their visit. Click here for details. Guests must also present a REAL ID-compliant photo identification upon arrival at the gate. Admission to the museum is free, and standard operating hours are Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
